transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-28 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Praxis Head of Security), Tom Nguyen (CTO), Aisha Khan (Lead ML Engineer)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intro — I’m Jordan, AE on the account, and Samir is our SE who'll handle the technical bits.
[00:12] Lena: Hi all, Lena here. We want to run through your security posture, SOC2, iso, SSO and how data is retained — basically make sure we can go production.
[00:20] Tom: Yeah hi, Tom. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary drivers are data residency, auditability, and key management.
[00:28] Samir: Great, that's exactly what we'll focus on. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM, RBAC and tenant isolation, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS and BYOK, plus deletion and data residency. Sound good?
[00:39] Aisha: Yep. Also want to understand any KV cache or prefix caching implications for PHI — we have some sensitive telemetry.
[00:47] Jordan: Noted. One thing up front: for hosted we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 coverage — we'll share the certs after the call. For regulated workloads many customers choose Dedicated or Private for extra isolation and optional customer-managed keys.
[01:00] Lena: Can you confirm the SOC scope? Does it include the inference runtime and customer data handling?
[01:06] Jordan: Yes, SOC2 scope covers the API, control plane and logs handling for hosted. For Dedicated, the contract provides additional commitments and we can include specific controls in the SOW.
[01:15] Tom: For iso, are you certified currently? Which standard?
[01:18] Jordan: ISO 27001 is in place — we'll send the scope doc. Samir, want to add detail on separation for Dedicated/Private?
[01:24] Samir: Sure. For Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools in a tenant-isolated network. We support VPC peering and private link to avoid public egress. For Private we can do a customer-managed control plane in their VPC or on-prem with air-gapped option. There are tradeoffs on latency and ops burden.
[01:40] Lena: How about SSO? We use SAML 2.0 with Okta and SCIM provisioning. Need role mapping and RBAC tied to groups.
[01:48] Samir: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC; SCIM provisioning for users/groups is supported. RBAC is role based with admin, ops, viewer, and model-deploy roles. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. There's also API keys for machine-to-machine, which can be scoped.
[02:02] Aisha: Are API keys stored encrypted? Can we enforce rotation?
[02:06] Samir: Keys are encrypted at rest; rotation tooling exists and we recommend short-lived tokens for automation. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your KMS for secrets.
[02:15] Tom: KMS — do you support BYOK and HSM-backed keys?
[02:19] Samir: Yes. For hosted we offer integration with major cloud KMS providers and BYOK where we can wrap the data encryption keys with your key. For Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS or HSM via IAM, or use customer-managed keys in your VPC. Caveat: fully on-prem HSM requires Private deployment and extra setup.
[02:33] Lena: Audit logs — how granular are they? We need per-request metadata, who invoked, model used, latency and the request id for tracing. Also retention configurable.
[02:42] Samir: Audit logs include user, API key, route, model version, request id, timestamp, p95 latency and error codes. By default logs are retained 90 days on hosted; for enterprise tiers we offer longer retention and can stream logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or S3 with encryption. For Dedicated/Private you control retention and can ship logs to your infra.
[03:00] Lena: Can we get immutable audit trail for compliance?
[03:03] Samir: You can export logs to an immutable store (e.g., S3 with WORM policies) on your side; we also provide signed log export options.
[03:12] Tom: Data residency — we need EU-only for some tenants. How do you guarantee region isolation?
[03:18] Jordan: We offer region-restricted deployments; for hosted you can pin to specific cloud region and we can restrict routing. For Dedicated and Private you control the region entirely.
[03:27] Aisha: On the inference path, does Redwood cache prefixes or KV in a way that could leak PII across tenants?
[03:33] Samir: Good question. KV cache is tenant-isolated; we do not share cache across tenants. For hosted, prefix caching is scoped per-tenant and per-model version. There are safeguards for redaction but customers with strict workloads often choose Dedicated/Private to remove any multi-tenant risk.
[03:50] Lena: What about model telemetry — are prompts and generated outputs stored? What's the retention and can we disable storage?
[03:57] Jordan: By default we persist logs used for billing and quality monitoring for X days (we'll put exact numbers in the pack). For enterprise agreements you can opt out of telemetry retention or choose to have telemetry stored only in your VPC. We also support purge requests and retention policies at the org or route level.
[04:13] Lena: We need legal controls for deletion and e-discovery. Can you process formal data deletion requests within a contractually agreed SLA?
[04:20] Jordan: Yes, deletion and data subject requests can be included in the contract; we have workflows and audit trails for deletion events.
[04:27] Tom: Encryption in transit and at rest?
[04:30] Samir: TLS 1.2/1.3 for transit, and AES-256 for rest with KMS wrapping. For BYOK the data keys are wrapped with your key.
[04:38] Aisha: Any limitations on model types for private deploys? We run some custom fine-tuned models; we'd want to host our own model artifacts.
[04:45] Samir: Private and some Dedicated plans allow you to bring model artifacts; we have an onboarding flow for large model transfer and registry. We also support pinned model versions and can run your quantized artifacts. There's a security checklist for model artifact signing.
[04:59] Lena: Incident response — what's your process and SLAs for breaches?
[05:02] Jordan: We have an incident response policy, customers get notifications via the console and email, SLA for incident acknowledgement and updates is included in enterprise contracts. We'll share the IR playbook and MSA excerpts.
[05:13] Tom: For procurement — we'll need the security pack, pen test summary, and any third party attestation.
[05:18] Jordan: We'll send the security pack after this call (SOC2, ISO, pentest summary redacted as needed).
[05:24] Aisha: Performance question: if we move to dedicated GPUs, how do you guarantee p95? Is it part of the SLA or more empirical?
[05:31] Samir: Dedicated gives predictable throughput; latency SLOs are part of the Dedicated offering. We'll run a benchmark with your payload to validate p95 under your batch sizes and sequence lengths.
[05:42] Lena: Are there any regulatory certifications for healthcare or financial data beyond SOC2/ISO?
[05:47] Jordan: We support HIPAA workflows and BAAs for certain deployments; for financial we can discuss contractual confidentiality and additional controls.
[05:54] Tom: For SSO provisioning — can we enforce SCIM de-provisioning automation and immediate session termination?
[05:59] Samir: SCIM de-provisioning is supported; session termination for active tokens can be enforced by revoking sessions and rotating keys — there's a small propagation window for long-lived tokens. We recommend short-lived tokens where possible.
[06:12] Aisha: One last question — audits: can our auditors get read-only access into logs during a compliance review?
[06:17] Samir: Yes, we can provide time-limited read-only access or export the logs to your environment for the auditor.
[06:24] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps. We'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO, pentest summary), Samir will follow up to schedule the dedicated/VPC deep dive and architecture, Praxis will send sample payloads and retention/SLO requirements, and we'll scope pricing for a pilot.
[06:41] Lena: That works for us. Thanks everyone.
[06:44] Tom: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[06:47] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up by end of week.

Notes on transcript quality: some transcription noise — 'KV cash' or 'KV cache' mis-typed occasionally, proper nouns like Praxis sometimes mis-capitalized. References/links mentioned: security pack (link to be emailed), dedicated architecture doc (redwood.link/dedicated-arch), SOC2 and ISO certs (will be attached).
